item.title: Re: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Adding to that the preceding line, it would be significantly better without poor behavioral logic like:

This instance was opened by researchers (survivors reported sounds from inside the case as their reason for forgoing typical precautions)

I would think that sounds suddenly coming from inside the case would call for more precautions, not fewer.

Also, seconding the notion that it held back what could have made it great.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
This article is being placed up for review. Check it out, it needs more attention.

Once again, this one is just holding back on the good stuff. It's all building up to some weird shit being up in this luggage, and then when we actually get there, it's… kind of a letdown. The author really had the chance to go wild here, but held themselves back. I'm really growing weary of articles that are all buildup to some [DATA EXPUNGEF]. I mean… look at this bit.

releasing [DATA EXPUNGED], which caused substantial damage to the conveyor system area and the deaths of two on-site personnel. Despite the scale of the event, SCP-985 itself was undamaged, and the remains of the [DATA EXPUNGED] were unable to be recovered.

This article would be significantly better without expungement like that.

Heh - there are four possibilities there i guess.

Not dangerous -> becomes dangerous close up - This.
Dangerous -> becomes benign when investigated - SCP-EX type stuff
Not dangerous -> not dangerous - Tickle monster
Dangerous -> dangerous - About half SCP's
